title: Swap and swappiness
subtitle: Disk overflow for RAM — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Disk space used as overflow when RAM is full; inactive pages move there
cards.notes: Helps low-RAM machines; not a replacement for more RAM. Btrfs does not support swap.

cards.meaning: Partition recommended (contiguous); file more flexible without repartitioning
cards.notes: Can combine both. Kernel 2.6+ swap files nearly as fast if contiguous.

cards.meaning: Show RAM and swap usage in human-readable units
Kernel weight: swap cold app pages vs drop page cache (range 0–100, default 60)
cards.notes: High = happy to swap; low = protect app RAM, evict cache first

cards.meaning: Format a device or file as swap (never mkfs.ext4 on a swap LV)
Activate a swap device or file now
Deactivate swap before removing it — never rm an active swap file
Add swap as an LVM LV: create LV, format as swap, persist in fstab, activate
Create an empty file to use as swap (then mkswap, chmod 0600, fstab, swapon)
cards.notes: 64 MB = 64*1024 blocks; chmod 0600 — may hold RAM secrets

cards.meaning: Recommended swap = 2× RAM; with hibernation = 3× RAM
cards.notes: Bigger RAM: table drops toward ≥4 GB; hibernation needs ≥ RAM

cards.meaning: Persist swap across reboot: device/file swap swap defaults 0 0
